_comment: Topic collation (Task 16.5): the third, fourth and fifth link on Marathon training. links: what the store sends; output: a saved answer in the TopicResult shape.

links.title: A 16-week marathon plan
links.line: Builds from 30 to 70 km a week with a cut-back every fourth week.

links.title: Why easy runs should be easy
links.line: Most running should be at a conversational pace.

links.title: Strength work for runners
links.line: Two short strength sessions a week reduce injury.

links.title: Taper myths
links.line: A two-week taper is enough for most amateurs.

links.title: Fuelling long runs
links.line: Practise race-day food on long runs.

output.summary: Five pieces on preparing for a marathon. The plan builds weekly distance slowly with regular cut-back weeks, most runs stay easy, strength work twice a week keeps injuries away, a two-week taper is enough, and race food should be practised on long runs.

notes.note: The backbone: a 16-week plan with cut-back weeks.
Why most runs in the plan should be easy.
Adds two strength sessions a week.
Settles the taper at two weeks.
Food on long runs, which the plan does not cover.

overlaps: The plan and the taper piece agree on two weeks of tapering
open_questions: Which spring marathon, and how many weeks away is it?
output.next_step: Pick the race date and count back 16 weeks.
